skill.description: Generate and edit images with GPT Image 2 through the local Codex CLI. The skill uses the user's ChatGPT subscription for text prompts, reference images, style transfer, and image extraction.
skill.summary: Generate GPT Image 2 images through Codex using a local ChatGPT subscription.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms legitimate but sensitive behavior: the skill invokes Codex CLI, sends prompts and reference images through the user's login, and reads generated payloads from ~/.codex/sessions. Most Markdown backtick, URL, temporary-file, device-file, and gallery PNG findings are false positives. The main residual risk is privacy exposure from hidden Codex session files and race-prone session discovery.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer an official Codex output path or API that writes the generated image directly. Avoid traversing ~/.codex/sessions when a direct output channel exists.
Use a unique session identifier, isolated session directory, or file lock so only the session created by this invocation is read.

remediation.issue: External processing through the user account
remediation.suggestion: Require clear user consent before running codex exec and disclose that prompts and reference images are processed by Codex and OpenAI.

remediation.issue: Binary gallery assets require manual trust
remediation.suggestion: Keep gallery PNGs small, retain provenance metadata, and remove unnecessary embedded metadata if it is not needed for marketplace display.

semantic_findings.title: Race-Prone Codex Session File Selection
semantic_findings.description: The wrapper diffs the entire ~/.codex/sessions tree before and after generation, then scans every new rollout file. A concurrent Codex session could be included and expose unrelated generated content or prompts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script collects all new rollout files by directory diff without a lock or unique session identifier. The README claims prior files are not touched, but the implementation can still include unrelated concurrent files.

semantic_findings.title: External Codex CLI Invocation Uses Local Account
semantic_findings.description: The script sends the generation instruction, raw prompt, and optional reference images to codex exec using the local logged-in account. This is expected for the skill, but it is a real external processing path for user data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script builds a codex exec command with image generation enabled and pipes the raw instruction to it. The documentation also states outbound traffic occurs through the Codex CLI to OpenAI.

content.user_title: Generate GPT Image 2 Assets from Claude Code
content.value_statement: Agents often need GPT Image 2 without setting up API keys. This skill runs local Codex CLI image generation using the user's ChatGPT subscription.
actual_capabilities: Runs GPT Image 2 generation through the local Codex CLI.
Creates images from plain text prompts.
Uses one or more reference images for edits and style transfer.
Writes the generated image to a caller-selected local output path.
Extracts image payloads from new Codex session rollout files.
Returns clear exit codes for missing tools, missing references, and failed generation.
limitations: Requires Codex CLI, local login, and a ChatGPT plan with image access.
Depends on Codex session files being persisted under the user profile.
Does not provide direct OpenAI API access or separate billing controls.
Uses an image generation feature flag that may change with Codex releases.

use_cases.title: Create concept visuals
use_cases.description: Generate draft images from text prompts for mood boards, campaigns, and product concepts.

use_cases.title: Restyle existing assets
use_cases.description: Use a reference image to create a new version with a requested visual style.

use_cases.title: Produce prototype imagery
use_cases.description: Create quick app, landing page, or documentation visuals while working inside an agent session.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a simple image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 to create a square illustration of a clean workspace with soft daylight. Save it as workspace.png.

prompt_templates.title: Edit one reference image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 with this reference image. Keep the layout, but change the style to watercolor packaging art.

prompt_templates.title: Combine multiple references
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 with both reference images. Match the first image layout and apply the second image color palette.

prompt_templates.title: Create a production-ready asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 to create a 16:9 launch banner with concise headline text, high contrast, and space for a product screenshot.

output_examples.input: Generate a poster for a new analytics feature using GPT Image 2.
output_examples.output: A local PNG poster is created at the requested path and can be attached in the agent response.

output_examples.input: Restyle this logo reference as a vintage travel badge.
output_examples.output: A new image file preserves the main shape while changing texture, palette, and illustration style.

output_examples.input: Create a product mockup from two reference images.
output_examples.output: The skill sends both references to Codex and extracts the generated mockup from the new session file.

best_practices: State the desired output path, aspect ratio, and visual style before running generation.
Use reference images only when the user has rights to process them.
Review prompts and references because they are processed through the logged-in Codex account.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill without a working Codex CLI login and image entitlement.
Do not send confidential reference images unless the user accepts the external processing path.
Do not expect this skill to bypass Codex quotas, model safety rules, or subscription limits.

faq.question: Does this skill need an OpenAI API key?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local Codex CLI and the user's existing ChatGPT subscription.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts repeatable reference images for edits, restyling, and multi-reference composition.

faq.question: Where does the generated image go?
faq.answer: The caller provides an output path. The extractor writes the generated image bytes to that path.

faq.question: Does it read Codex session files?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads new Codex session rollout files to find the generated image payload.

faq.question: Does it make network requests itself?
faq.answer: The shell script does not call custom endpoints. Codex performs the image generation request through the user's login.

faq.question: Can it run without Codex?
faq.answer: No. Codex CLI and python3 must be available on the local machine.
